skills.name: Properties of substances related to bond type and structure

note.text:
Bond type and structure decide physical properties:
• Ionic lattice: high m.p.; conducts when molten or dissolved; often soluble in water; brittle.
• Simple molecular: low m.p./b.p.; does not conduct; often insoluble in water, soluble in organic solvents.
• Giant covalent: very high m.p.; hard (diamond) or slippery (graphite); does not conduct (except graphite); insoluble.
• Metallic: high m.p. (usually); conducts when solid and liquid; malleable and ductile; insoluble.
Use test results (melting point, conductivity, solubility) to identify the structure of an unknown substance.

sections.heading: Structure explains properties
sections.text:
Every property you test in the laboratory comes back to the particles and the forces between them.
• Strong forces throughout a giant structure → high melting point.
• Weak forces between small molecules → low melting point.
• Charged particles that can move → electrical conductivity.

sections.heading: The four patterns
sections.text:
• Ionic: high m.p.; conducts only when molten or dissolved; often soluble in water; brittle.
• Simple molecular: low m.p.; never conducts; often insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
• Giant covalent: very high m.p.; insoluble; does not conduct (graphite is the exception).
• Metallic: usually high m.p.; conducts as solid and liquid; malleable and ductile; insoluble.

sections.heading: Identifying an unknown
sections.text:
Test three things: melting point, conductivity (solid, molten, in solution) and solubility.
Conducts when solid → metallic (or graphite). Conducts only when molten or dissolved → ionic. Low melting point and never conducts → simple molecular. Very high melting point, insoluble, does not conduct → giant covalent.

key_words.meaning: the temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid
how well a substance lets electricity through

mistake.wrong: All substances with high melting points are ionic
mistake.right: Giant covalent and metallic substances also have high melting points
mistake.why: Use conductivity too: it separates ionic, metallic and giant covalent substances.

worked_example.problem: Substance X melts at {1083} °C, conducts electricity as a solid and is ductile. Identify its structure.
steps: Conducts as a solid: only metals (and graphite) do this.
Ductile: metals can be drawn into wires.
So X is metallic (it is copper).

example: Copper and graphite conduct as solids.

cards.idea: Conducts only when molten or dissolved: ionic.
example: Molten salt conducts; solid salt does not.

cards.idea: Low melting point and no conduction: simple molecular.

pick.q: A white solid melts at 186 °C, does not conduct and dissolves in water. It is most likely…
e: Giant covalent substances melt much higher and are insoluble.
pick.y: Low melting point and no conduction: molecular.

pick.q: Which substance has the lowest melting point?
e: Diamond has very strong covalent bonds throughout.
pick.y: Only weak forces hold methane molecules together.

pick.q: Why does sulphur not conduct electricity, even when molten?
pick.r: It is made of molecules with no ions or free electrons
e: It is a solid at room temperature.

pick.q: Which substance conducts electricity when solid?

e: All of diamond's electrons are in bonds.
pick.y: Graphite has one free electron per carbon atom.

pick.q: A substance conducts both when solid and when molten. It is most likely…
e: Solid ionic compounds do not conduct.
pick.y: Free electrons conduct in both states.

pick.q: Which result shows that a substance is ionic?
pick.r: It conducts when molten but not when solid
e: Ionic compounds melt at high temperatures.
pick.y: Ions are free to move only in the melt or solution.

pick.q: Potassium iodide dissolves in water and the solution conducts. KI is…
e: It is a compound of a metal and a non-metal; it dissolves, unlike metals.
Its solution conducts, so it has ions.
pick.y: A metal + non-metal compound that conducts in solution.

pick.q: Why is magnesium oxide used to line furnaces?
pick.r: Its ionic lattice gives a very high melting point
e: Hardness and high melting point are needed.
pick.y: Strong ionic bonds withstand the heat.

pick.q: A white solid melts at 186 °C, does not conduct and dissolves in water. It is most likely…
e: Giant covalent substances melt much higher and are insoluble.
pick.y: Low melting point and no conduction: molecular.

pick.q: Which substance has the lowest melting point?
e: Diamond has very strong covalent bonds throughout.
pick.y: Only weak forces hold methane molecules together.

pick.q: Why does sulphur not conduct electricity, even when molten?
pick.r: It is made of molecules with no ions or free electrons
e: It is a solid at room temperature.

pick.q: Which set of properties fits an ionic compound?
pick.r: high m.p., soluble in water, conducts in solution
w: high m.p., conducts as a solid, malleable
very high m.p., insoluble, never conducts
e: That fits a simple molecular substance.
That fits a giant covalent substance such as diamond.
pick.y: Ionic: strong bonds, ions free in solution.

pick.q: Which set of properties fits a giant covalent substance like sand?
pick.r: very high m.p., insoluble, does not conduct
pick.y: Many strong covalent bonds and no free charges.

pick.q: Which set of properties fits a metal?
pick.r: conducts as a solid, malleable, usually high m.p.
